Cost of hiring a virtual assistant

Use discovery to define a scope you can compare: the tasks, capacity, coverage, specialist skills and review responsibilities.

Describe your taskSee what shapes a quote

What affects virtual assistant pricing

Virtual assistant pricing depends on hours and scope. Compare virtual assistant rates against the same workload.

Time and coverage

Expected volume, regular hours, time zone overlap and how quickly a task needs attention.

Skills and complexity

The systems involved, the level of specialist input and whether work spans several functions.

Setup and oversight

Documentation, onboarding, quality review, reporting and access setup. See what the first handoff involves.

Compare scope and terms together.

Ask what virtual assistant rates include before comparing quotes. The cost of hiring a virtual assistant also depends on setup, review and changes in the work.

Capacity

Hours or expected volume; overage rules; time zone and coverage.

Included work

Tasks, deliverables, tools, reviews and approval limits.

Fees and billing

Currency, billing period, setup fees and any specialist or tool charges.

Changes and continuity

How scope changes, handovers, unused capacity and gaps in coverage are handled.

Commitment

Start date, renewal, notice and cancellation terms.

Two ways to define the work

Compare virtual assistant hourly rates for the same tasks. Virtual assistant pricing varies with review needs.

Recurring admin

A daily inbox review and a weekly calendar check. Estimate typical volume, time zone overlap and how often an approval is needed.

Content publication

An approved article queue. Define expected volume, formatting and on-page checks, and which changes need specialist review.

Bring enough detail for a useful quote.

Estimate the cost of hiring a virtual assistant using normal and busy periods. Virtual assistant pricing should account for the questions that take extra review time.

Know when to revisit the quote.

Review virtual assistant rates when the workload or coverage changes. Virtual assistant hourly rates alone do not describe what happens when a queue exceeds its scope.

A temporary peak

If an event or launch increases volume, define the extra work and the dates it applies to.

A recurring change

If an additional queue becomes part of the regular workload, revisit capacity and assign someone to review the output.

A higher-risk task

If the work needs broader permissions or a new approval rule, review how to approve access changes before expanding the scope.

Estimate the cost of hiring a virtual assistant

Virtual assistant pricing becomes easier to estimate with a small sample. Compare the cost of hiring a virtual assistant against the execution and review time that sample requires.

Estimate workload by request type

Use examples of the work rather than one total for the whole queue. A template reply, a scheduling conflict and a request that needs approval can take different amounts of time and involve different owners.

Compare virtual assistant rates with setup included

Account for the first batch, walkthroughs and changes to instructions. Ask which setup work is included and how ongoing reviews are scheduled once the workflow is stable.

Review virtual assistant hourly rates and coverage

A smaller queue may still need a regular response window. Show whether a deadline applies to every item or only urgent requests, and note the time zone and days that matter.

Compare virtual assistant hourly rates and coverage

Compare virtual assistant hourly rates alongside availability and the work included. The cost of hiring a virtual assistant should also reflect any specialist input.

A regular brief

Useful when the inputs are predictable and one person reviews the output. Agree the schedule and what should happen if a request is too urgent for the next brief.

A shared queue

Useful when work arrives throughout an agreed coverage window. Define which categories are in scope, how items are prioritised and how unresolved work is handed to the next owner.

A connected set of tasks

Useful when more than one team contributes to a finished result. Ask whether handoffs, review, documentation and changes are included in the proposed capacity.

Check the proposal against the actual workflow.

Check virtual assistant pricing against the tasks your team actually needs. Virtual assistant rates should be accompanied by a clear scope and approval for changes.

Check the starting conditions

Ask what needs to be in place on day one, such as access to a queue, approved templates or an available reviewer. Identify which delay would change the timing of the first output.

Check the change route

Look for a clear way to add work, reduce volume or change coverage. Agree who can request the change and when a revised scope takes effect.

Check the handover

Confirm what happens to instructions, open items and access if the scope ends or moves to another person. Identify the record that will show the final status.

Share the details that affect the estimate.

Provide the same details when requesting virtual assistant rates. Virtual assistant pricing is easier to compare when the volumes, tools and deadlines match.

Explain the busy periods

Show what changes during events, launches or reporting deadlines. Indicate whether extra demand is temporary or part of the normal workload.

Identify approval work

Give a name or role for the person who reviews changes and decisions. Include any checks that must happen before a message is sent, a record changes or a page goes live.

Ask how it will be reviewed

Agree when to compare the estimate with actual work. Use a small sample of finished items and exceptions to see which assumptions need updating.

Compare two scopes using the same workload.

Compare the cost of hiring a virtual assistant under different coverage windows. Virtual assistant hourly rates need to be read alongside the time reserved for the queue.

A scheduled review window

The assistant checks the queue at agreed times, handles approved replies and collects exceptions for one review. This works when requests can wait for the next window and the manager can clear the decision list in one pass.

Coverage across more of the day

The assistant checks more often and flags time-sensitive cases as they arrive. Ask who is available to review those cases, whether the extra checks need specialist skills and how gaps in coverage are handled.

What to compare on the quote

Use the same weekly volume, peak volume and expected result for both scopes. Ask which time is included for onboarding, documenting the work and coordinating approvals so both proposals describe the same level of service.

Ask how the quote handles a busy month.

Ask how virtual assistant pricing handles predictable peaks. Virtual assistant rates for additional work should have a clear approval route before the busy period.

Known busy periods

Mark events, campaigns or monthly deadlines on the calendar. Share a previous busy week if one is available so the estimate reflects both the extra work and the dates when a reviewer is available.

Unexpected requests

Ask which work can wait until the normal window, what can be paused and who can approve extra capacity. A named approval contact makes it easier to handle the immediate queue without guessing about cost.

Work that needs a specialist

Point out requests involving specialist systems or decisions, such as a tracking change or a mass record update. Ask whether that work should be priced separately and which team member reviews it.

Review the quote against the first month’s work.

Review virtual assistant rates after the first complete work cycle. Use the actual volume and review time to see whether the original quote still fits.

Actual volume and timing

Count completed and blocked requests separately, then compare the total with what was estimated. Check when the requests arrived so a steady weekly count does not hide a busy day that needs different coverage.

Work that takes longer

Look at items that required several messages, a second reviewer or additional information. Decide whether to improve the instructions, move that task out of scope or adjust the amount of time allowed for it.

Changes and approvals

Write down which assumptions changed and get the revised scope reviewed before the next cycle. Keep the decision and start date with the quote so the team can compare like for like later.

Frequently Asked Questions

Ask what changes virtual assistant pricing before requesting a quote. Virtual assistant hourly rates should be considered with the review process and expected coverage.

How is support priced?

The proposed scope should account for capacity, specialist skills, schedule and any setup or reporting needs. Ask for those items to be listed separately.

What if my workload changes?

Ask how extra work is approved, billed or rescheduled, and what happens to unused capacity.

Is there a minimum commitment?

Check the minimum term, notice period and cancellation rules in the proposed agreement.

What information makes a quote more useful?

Share normal and peak volumes, the tools involved, coverage windows and examples of routine and unusual requests. Virtual assistant pricing is easier to compare when each proposal uses the same workload and expected result.

Do hourly rates include setup and review time?

Ask for setup, execution, reporting and review responsibilities to be stated in the scope. When comparing virtual assistant hourly rates, check which activities are included and who approves any extra work or specialist input.

How should we compare two proposals?

Compare the tasks, expected volume, coverage and approval responsibilities together. The cost of hiring a virtual assistant should be considered alongside the output you receive and the time your own team will spend providing input and reviewing work.

Make room for the work only you can do.

Tell us which task you’d like to hand off and what a good result looks like. Start with one piece of work that comes up regularly.
